title: GeoSticky allocator with throttled evacuation and residency preflight checks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a regional placement allocator (GeoSticky) for dedicated fleets that enforces data residency constraints while providing throughput guarantees and controlled failover. The allocator must: 1) prefer region-anchored pools for customer commitments, 2) maintain throughput 'slices' per commitment with soft and hard scaling behavior, 3) run residency preflight checks before scheduled spillover to other regions or zones, and 4) perform throttled evacuation to avoid sudden capacity loss for customers during zone failures or maintenance windows. This ticket covers design, prototype scheduler, simulator runs, and a minimal control-plane integration for canary rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Allocator schedules new workloads with region affinity > 90% when capacity available
Throughput slices honor committed qps within 5% under steady state
When a zone drains, evacuation rate is throttled to configured bandwidth and fallbacks respect residency flags
Residency preflight rejects cross-region spillover when customer policy = 'strict' and logs actionable rejection reason
Automated simulator demonstrates median failover latency reduction vs naive spillover by >= 20%
Control-plane exposes placement decisions and reason codes in Console for auditing
engineering_notes: Core idea: maintain per-customer allocation token buckets (slices) that track committed throughput and current headroom. Use a prioritized knapsack-style bin-packing across zone candidates to satisfy slices while maximizing regional affinity.
Soft scaling: allow transient exceed of region slice by up to X% for up to Y minutes, tracked per commitment. Hard scaling denies allocations beyond hard limit.
Evacuation throttling: implement drain windows with configurable max concurrent migrations and a backoff policy to avoid pile-up on remaining zones.

Residency preflight: evaluate candidate target based on (1) region tag, (2) customer residency policy enum, (3) legal blocklist, (4) data movement cost estimate. Preflight returns pass/fail and human-readable reason code.
Compatibility: allocator must interoperate with existing autoscaler (ENG-31222) and commitment mapper (ENG-246801). Provide feature-flagged rollout.
Observability: emit placement_reason, residency_decision, slice_consumption, evacuation_rate metrics. Add trace hooks for end-to-end sampling.
testing_plan: Unit tests for knapsack placer and slice accounting
End-to-end integration in staging with synthetic traffic shapes that mimic bursty enterprise workloads
Fault injection: simulate zone drain and verify evacuation throttling and failback correctness
Fidelity check: replay 30 days of historical placement traces to measure affinity and spillover frequency
rollout_plan: Feature flag gating: off by default; enable for internal test orgs
Canary stage: 5% of new dedicated pool creations routed through GeoSticky allocator
Metrics gate: only promote if slice SLA and failover latency targets met for 48h
Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 3-week window with abort thresholds
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-optimizing for affinity could underutilize capacity. Mitigation: implement global fallback lane with controlled preemption and cost accounting.
Risk: Complex residency logic increases decision latency. Mitigation: cache residency evaluations per customer-region pair and use async preflight for non-blocking allocations.
Risk: Evacuation throttling may prolong degraded performance during outages. Mitigation: expose emergency override for SRE to increase throttles temporarily and track cost impact.
Risk: Incorrect accounting could violate customer commitments. Mitigation: add reconciliation job that verifies slice consumption against invoices and alerts anomalies.
